query: What business models and customers do these companies describe?

per_column.name: primary_business_model
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the 'business models' part of the query and provides a clean categorical axis to group companies. Samples are well-grounded: VC firms tagged vc_investment, 280 Group tagged consulting, 23andMe as software_platform is a defensible reading of a personalized-reports product. Values follow soundly from the descriptions.

per_column.name: primary_customer_segment
per_column.rationale: Directly addresses the 'customers' part of the query and gives a genuine grouping axis. Consumer/enterprise assignments are mostly reasonable (23andMe consumer, Addepar enterprise). However VC firms labeled 'enterprise' is a somewhat loose inference since their customers/investees aren't explicitly enterprise; still defensible but not strongly supported by the text.

per_column.name: service_delivery_mode
per_column.rationale: A useful new axis distinct from business model. But groundedness is weak in samples: both VC firms are labeled 'api_based', which the descriptions do not support at all and is essentially invented. 280 Group's training/consulting labeled 'cloud_saas' is also unwarranted. Delivery mode is often not stated in these short descriptions, yet confident specifics were produced.

per_column.name: industry_focus
per_column.rationale: Strong analytical leverage for comparing sectors across companies. Mostly well-grounded: 5AM/life science to healthcare_biotech, Addepar to enterprise_data. 23andMe as 'consumer_marketplace' is a slightly off fit (it's more health/genomics), and 280 Group as education_training is reasonable given training/certification mention.

per_column.name: value_proposition_type
per_column.rationale: Adds a distinct modeling axis on why customers buy. Addepar to analytics_insight and 23andMe to user_experience are sound readings. VC firms mapped to revenue_growth (returns to investors) is defensible. 280 Group to efficiency_automation is a weaker inference from a proven-process claim but not contradictory.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively give strong, non-redundant analytical leverage for a query about business models and customers: business model, customer segment, industry, value proposition, and delivery mode each offer a distinct grouping/comparison axis. Groundedness is generally good but dragged down by service_delivery_mode, which fabricates confident specifics (e.g., 'api_based' for venture capital firms) where the source text is silent. Other columns are mostly sound readings of the descriptions, with only minor loose inferences.
